name: Bubble Break ASMR Tabletop
request: Create a small, playable Bubble Break ASMR game for one player on desktop and touch. The player presses individual bubbles on a reusable bubble-wrap sheet. A press visibly depresses and pops that bubble with synchronized satisfying pop audio, then adds exactly one to the popped counter after the pop completes. Holding, spamming, or pressing a popped bubble must not count twice. Let the player finish a sheet of at least twelve bubbles, see completion feedback, and deliberately reset to a fresh sheet. Use a close, readable tabletop presentation and minimal counter/reset UI. Search Marketplace first for a complete reusable interaction, including any existing geometry, animation, sounds and behavior; inspect what it already provides and integrate only missing features. Search separately for missing media if needed. Audio must come from Marketplace and actually play. Record unavailable importer capabilities rather than pretending a suitable scripted component does not exist. Choose reasonable details yourself; no saving, multiplayer, purchases or large map. Success needs observed press/pop/recovery timing, per-bubble state, exact counting, sheet completion/reset and usable desktop/touch input. Do not claim success from code inspection alone.

spec.assetStrategy:
Begin with Model discovery for a complete bubble-wrap popping interaction, not a static sheet or generic prop. Inspect candidate hierarchies and all reusable geometry, scripts, state machines, animation/tween behavior, interaction inputs, reset logic, UI hooks, and embedded media before assigning implementation ownership. Preserve useful verified behavior and integrate only the requirements demonstrably absent from the retained component. Because the imported interface is unknown until inspection, discovery-dependent integration tasks intentionally have no preassigned script paths.

The complete component need is optional in the acquisition sense: an unsuccessful audited search may enter the bounded fallback policy, but discovery cannot be skipped, and importer or unsupported-script limitations must be escalated as capability gaps rather than treated as evidence that no component exists. Standalone animation acquisition is not assumed; compatible animation must be inspected within Models, while any later authored visual fallback requires recorded unsuccessful sourcing and approval under the fallback policy.

Pop audio is independently mandatory and Marketplace-only. First inspect and capture relevant sound references from the retained complete component. If none is suitable, conduct the separate Audio search declared above. In either case, provenance, loading, actual playback, audibility, and synchronization must pass native checks. Failure to obtain or verify usable audio blocks completion; no generated, procedural, built-in, placeholder, or invented audio may substitute. Supporting tabletop construction should remain authored scene composition unless the retained component already includes useful safe presentation elements; no unrelated Marketplace decoration is needed.
spec.title: Bubble Break ASMR Tabletop
spec.summary:
A compact, single-player bubble-wrap popping experience centered on one reusable 4-by-4 sheet with 16 individually pressable bubbles. The player spawns beside a safe, collidable tabletop station with the entire sheet immediately visible at close range. A short visual cue and minimal instruction invite a mouse click or touch tap. Each valid press visibly compresses one bubble, reaches a distinct pop moment with synchronized Marketplace audio, settles into a clearly collapsed state, and only then increases the counter by exactly one. Locked per-bubble state prevents holds, rapid repeats, overlapping inputs, and already-popped bubbles from scoring again. After all 16 bubbles are popped, completion feedback appears and a deliberate reset control creates a fresh unpopped sheet and returns the counter to zero.

The shared world is confined to Workspace/Forge_4692609c69a4 and consists of a small bounded tabletop vignette, a safe spawn, the central interaction sheet, and restrained supporting props or lighting. Server-owned state validates bubble identity, interaction distance, current phase, completion state, and request rate; the client owns device input and presentation while treating replicated state as authoritative. No saving, purchases, progression, multiplayer-specific competition, or large traversal space will be added. Respawn restores input and HUD bindings without duplicating interfaces or resetting the active sheet unexpectedly.

Marketplace discovery and inspection occur before replacement implementation. A complete reusable bubble-wrap interaction is preferred and must be audited for geometry, scripts, animation, input behavior, state handling, and embedded sound references. Only verified missing integration may be authored after that inspection. A separately declared Marketplace audio requirement remains mandatory even when the sound is captured from the retained component. Assumed defaults are 16 bubbles, a short approximately 0.15–0.30 second visible press/pop/settle sequence, a persistent collapsed final state, and a compact two-step reset confirmation to make reset deliberate. All interaction, audio, animation, exact-counting, completion, reset, desktop, and touch claims require observed native gameplay verification rather than code inspection.
spec.visualDirection:
Present the game as a close, softly lit tabletop ASMR vignette rather than an open map. The bubble sheet is the dominant focal object, centered on a warm matte wood or neutral craft surface and sized so all 16 bubbles remain readable from the starting view. Keep the spawn within roughly 6–8 studs of the interaction area, with a collidable floor and unobtrusive boundaries that prevent falling or wandering away. A desk lamp silhouette, shallow tray edge, or one restrained stationery grouping may frame the sheet, but decoration must not obscure bubble hit targets or compete with the interaction.

Use a calm hierarchy: warm low-saturation table and background colors, a translucent or pale cool-toned bubble sheet, brighter specular highlights on intact domes, and darker/flatter collapsed bubbles. Intact, pressing, popping, and popped states must be distinguishable through silhouette and height, not color alone. The press phase should show immediate downward travel or compression; the pop moment should have a crisp collapse and restrained highlight response; the settle phase should end in a stable recessed shape without regrowing the bubble. Completion can use a brief sheet-wide glow, soft border pulse, or concise banner, avoiding confetti or noisy effects that undermine the ASMR tone.

The HUD should occupy little screen space: a high-contrast counter such as “Popped 0 / 16” and one reset button in a safe corner, with touch-sized controls, restrained rounded panels, and no inventory or economy chrome. The reset confirmation should appear adjacent to the same control instead of opening a large modal. Input hover or selection feedback on desktop and clear touch-down feedback on mobile should identify the targeted bubble without delaying the physical response. Camera composition must keep the sheet close and legible while preserving normal device aspect ratios and avoiding GUI overlap.

tasks.title: Discover and audit a complete Marketplace bubble-wrap interaction before assigning replacement or glue scripts; inspect geometry, behavior sources, animation, sounds, dependencies, device input, and importer compatibility, and record every unsupported capability.
Select the relevant captured component sound or separately discover Marketplace pop audio, then verify provenance, loading, playback, audibility, and suitability for synchronization.

Compose the bounded tabletop vignette around the inspected component, including safe spawn, collidable surfaces, close interaction distance, readable sheet placement, restrained framing props, lighting, and unobstructed hit targets.

After inspection establishes retained interfaces, integrate only missing authoritative bubble state, validated requests, press/pop/settle phases, delayed exact counting, duplicate protection, synchronized verified audio, completion, and fresh-sheet reset. Register only necessary cohesive scripts at that stage.

Integrate desktop click and touch targeting plus the persistent minimal counter, completion feedback, and deliberate reset confirmation against the authoritative interfaces established by the retained component and core loop.
Add session cleanup and respawn rebinding around the inspected integration so character replacement cannot duplicate controls, HUDs, sounds, requests, or state listeners.

Run protected native desktop and touch verification of required instances, close tabletop readability, all action phases, Marketplace audio playback and synchronization, exact post-pop counting, spam resistance, full-sheet completion, confirmed reset, and respawn cleanup; report any missing asset or capability as blocked.
